occupations.title: Project Management Specialists
occupations.mapping: model-inferred from pack D (no review data)
occupations.rationale: Wrike is a project management tool with features like "Gantt chart," "Resource management," and "Task management" [D:Wrike:landing:7] used to "kick-start projects" and "Plan & resource" [D:Wrike:landing:6].

tasks.text: Report project status, such as budget, resources, technical issues, or customer satisfaction, to managers.
Create project status presentations for delivery to customers or project personnel.
Identify project needs such as resources, staff, or finances by reviewing project objectives and schedules.
Request and review project updates to ensure deadlines are met.

occupations.title: General and Operations Managers
occupations.mapping: model-inferred from pack D (no review data)
occupations.rationale: These managers use Wrike to gain "Optimal visibility across projects and departments," "Connect cross-functional teams," and "easily allocate resources" [D:Wrike:landing:6] to oversee business operations.

tasks.text: Review financial statements, sales or activity reports, or other performance data to measure productivity or goal achievement or to identify areas needing cost reduction or program improvement.
Monitor suppliers to ensure that they efficiently and effectively provide needed goods or services within budgetary limits.
Direct administrative activities directly related to making products or providing services.
Prepare staff work schedules and assign specific duties.

occupations.title: Management Analysts
occupations.mapping: model-inferred from pack D (no review data)
occupations.rationale: Management Analysts use Wrike's features for "Workflow automation" [D:Wrike:landing:6] and turning "raw work data into clear, actionable intelligence" [D:Wrike:landing:3] to analyze and improve business processes.

tasks.text: Prepare manuals and train workers in use of new forms, reports, procedures or equipment, according to organizational policy.
Review forms and reports and confer with management and users about format, distribution, and purpose, identifying problems and improvements.
Plan study of work problems and procedures, such as organizational change, communications, information flow, integrated production methods, inventory control, or cost analysis.
Analyze data gathered and develop solutions or alternative methods of proceeding.
